p: Eastbourne likes to call itself the sunshine coast, and it does have a good claim to some of the sunniest weather in the country. But even here, the weather doesn't always behave, and when the wind whips up along the seafront, everyone needs a plan B. A games bar is a great one, giving groups a warm, lively place to hide away and settle a few scores.

Eastbourne station is right in the town centre, with direct trains from London Victoria and along the south coast, so it's an easy trip for a day or weekend. The town is very walkable, with the shops, seafront and pier all within easy reach of each other.

It's a popular spot for celebrations, so if you're coming as part of a hen do, stag weekend or birthday trip, it's a smart idea to sort your games booking early. Plan an itinerary that mixes daytime seaside fun with an evening of games, and you'll keep everyone entertained without needing to drive anywhere.

For something completely different during the day, the Towner Eastbourne gallery is a striking modern building with changing exhibitions, and the Redoubt Fortress is a Napoleonic-era fort on the seafront that tells the story of the town's military past. If the weather's kind, the beach huts and promenade are perfect for a lazy afternoon. Just along the coast, Birling Gap gives you an easy way to see the Seven Sisters cliffs up close.
